summary: Proposes 'MicroSkill Architecture': project knowledge split into small skill capsules with guardrails and boilerplate, selected per task by a cosine-similarity router under a token budget, with a binary guardrail verifier on generated changes and a self-learning loop that extracts new capsules. A single case study on an enterprise CMS (15 features, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) compares it to dumping all docs and foundational source into context.

claims.claim: Token consumption cut by over 90% (48,500 -> 3,200 tokens per feature, ~93.4%).
claims.evidence: Table I, single run per feature, 15 features; baseline is a full-context dump, so a large reduction is expected by construction.
Table I; corresponds to 6/15 vs 13/15 features; no variance, no repeated runs, no significance test.
§IV-B: the guardrail verifier rejects out-of-scope writes before commit, so zero violations is guaranteed by the mechanism being measured; baseline had no equivalent check.

claims.claim: Self-learning loop autonomously extracted 7 reusable capsules.
claims.evidence: §IV-B narrative; no quality evaluation of extracted capsules beyond reuse anecdote.

patterns.note: Skill capsules loaded on demand; evidence from one case study vs a full-dump baseline.
Context allocation formalized as relevance maximization under a token budget.
Capsule-scoped write guardrails with binary verifier.
Self-learning loop that registers new capsules.

methodology.sample: One system (enterprise CMS), 15 feature specifications, within-subjects two conditions.
methodology.baselines: Monolithic context (all docs + directory + foundational files concatenated); no retrieval/RAG, AGENTS.md, or skills-based baseline.
methodology.ablations: None (router, guardrails, boilerplate, self-learning not separated).

standards.artifacts: None (no code, capsules, or CMS released).

biases.detail: Full-context dump is the weakest plausible comparator; no retrieval or curated-instructions baseline.
Violation count is enforced to zero by the guardrail being evaluated.
Authors' own framework on a CMS they presumably built, measured by their metrics.
Repackages progressive disclosure/skills + RAG routing under a microservices metaphor.
'eliminates architectural violations entirely', 'survive contact with reality'.

coi.affiliations: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at AriooBarzan Engineering Team, Shiraz, Iran (one author email at sutech.ac.ir).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: The authors' own framework; no commercial product named.
coi.detail: Company lab evaluating its own architecture without independent replication; no product sale evident.

verdict_reason: Evidence is a single unreplicated 15-feature case study with one model, a full-dump strawman baseline, no variance or ablations, a circular violations metric, unstated language, and no artifacts. The idea (on-demand skills + scoped guardrails) is reasonable but this paper does not provide evidence for it.
applicability: The idea of small, scoped knowledge capsules with write-scope guardrails is relevant to a Java team spreading ingestion over ≥4 repos (per-repo/per-module skills instead of one huge instruction file, deny writes to core modules), and fits hosts that support skills. But the numbers should not be used to justify the decision: the comparison is against dumping everything into context, which no team would do. Prefer evidence from controlled context-file/skill studies in the corpus.

conflicts_with.detail: MicroSkill reports large correctness gains from changing context strategy; the two-agent ablation reports context-injection strategy did not measurably move correctness (bounded ≤10-15pp) across 288 runs.
